brief: A note-taking app in 3D space — recent notes float near, old ones drift away, connections are threads

dominant_strengths: Depth metaphor of near/far notes via scale and opacity is conceptually clear and supports the temporal navigation brief
Restrained dark palette with single indigo accent gives connection threads visual primacy without chromatic noise
Legend in bottom-right ('Near ↔ Far') quietly teaches the spatial language without modal instruction
dominant_weaknesses: The Spatial Notes header card overlaps and occludes a primary note ('...es'), reading as a layout collision rather than intentional layering
Connection threads are inconsistent — some cards float disconnected, others have stub endpoints, breaking the 'threads = relationships' promise
Typographic hierarchy is flat: titles, body, and timestamps share too-similar weights/sizes, weakening the depth illusion that scale alone tries to carry
fix_priorities: Reposition the control panel so it never occludes notes, or make it a true floating HUD with backdrop blur and clear z-separation
Audit thread topology — every visible thread should terminate on a card, and depth should attenuate thread opacity in lockstep with the node
Strengthen typographic depth cues: blur, desaturate, and shrink distant cards more aggressively so 'old = far' is felt, not just labeled
Add subtle parallax/motion affordances on hover so the 3D space feels navigable rather than a static diagram
rationale.norman_balance: Reflective concept outpaces visceral polish and behavioral clarity — the idea intrigues but the execution doesn't yet invite confident interaction.
rationale.intent_fit: Partially solves the brief: the spatial-time metaphor is legible, but threads and depth falloff are too inconsistent to make the 3D notion feel inhabited.
